Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 14 January 2009 OILC NO. T MS. MARY ELEANOR A. MENDOZA Vice-President for Business Development Eton Properties Philippines, Inc. 12/F Allied Bank Center 6754 Ayala Avenue cor. Legaspi St. Makati City Dear Ms. Mendoza: This has reference to your earlier letter asking for our legal opinion on the scope of the review power of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Laguna over resolutions passed by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Sta. Rosa, a component city of that province. Per your letter, your company is developing a real estate project to be known as the "South Lake Village at Eton City" located in Barangay Malitlit, City of Sta. Rosa, Province of Laguna. You said that on 16 June 2008, the City of Sta. Rosa issued a Development Permit in your company's favor pursuant to Kapasiyahan No. 156-2008, dated 16 June 2008 of the Sangguniang Panlungsod, that city. In fact, you have attached to your letter a copy of the Development Permit signed by City Mayor Arlene ArciIIas-Nazareno. Surprisingly thereafter, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan has started to conduct hearings concerning the project and your company, as the developer of the project, was required to attend said hearings allegedly for purposes of review, confirmation and approval by that August Body of the said City Resolution. Meanwhile, according to you, the Sangguniang Panlungsod maintains a legal position that its City Resolution approving your company's Development Permit is not anymore subject to review, confirmation and approval by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan so that up to the date of your letter, the former has not officially transmitted to the latter the subject City Resolution and its attached documents. Thus, you are now seeking for our legal opinion on this issue: whether or not a resolution issued by a Sangguniang Panlungsod approving the issuance of a development permit for a residential/commercial subdivision is subject to review the Sangguniang Panlalawigan.

-2- In relation thereto, on 28 November 2008, you learned about the passage of Resolution No. 429, series of 2008 by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, entitled "Resolution Urging the Honorable Governor Teresita S Lazaro to Issue Cease and Desist Order to the Continuing Development Eton City at the City of Sta. Rosa, Laguna". According to you, the aforesaid Sangguniang Panlalawigan resolution was passed allegedly because the City Resolution approving your company's Development Permit as well as the Development Permit itself for the project has not been reviewed, confirmed and approved by that August Body. Hence, you posed an additional query for our resolution: whether or not the Sangguniang Panlalawigan or the Provincial Governor has the authority to issue a cease and desist order (CDO) against your company vis-å-vis your intended real estate project. In reply to your main query, may we invite your attention to Section 56 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), to wit: "SECTION 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang panlalawigan. Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and the resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils." It is clear from the foregoing that the power of review conferred unto the Sangguniang Panlalawigan extends only to approved city ordinances and resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils. Stated differently, all approved ordinances of the component cities are mandated by the Local Government Code to be forwarded to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review. On the other hand, resolutions are not anymore to be forwarded to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review except those resolutions approving and adopting the local development plans and public investment programs of component cities which, by express mandate of Section 56 (a) of the Local Government Code, are to be submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review. The rationale behind the exception given to resolutions approving and adopting the local development plans and public investment programs is that they pertain to matter with permanence and thus, in the nature of an Ordinance. At this juncture, it is imperative to distinguish an ordinance from a resolution, which are both products of our local legislative bodies such as the local sanggunians. "A municipal ordinance is different from a resolution. An ordinance is a law, but a resolution is merely a declaration of the sentiment or opinion of a lawmaking body on specific matter. An ordinance possesses a general and permanent character, but a resolution is temporary in nature. Additionally, the two are enacted differently — a third reading is necessary for an ordinance, but not for a resolution, unless decided otherwise by a

-3- majority of all the Sanggunian members" (Municipality Paranaque V.M. Realty Corporation, G.R. Ne., 127820, go July 1998). Going now to the subject Kapasiyahan No. 156-2008, dated 16 June 2008 of the Sangguniang Pantungsod of the City of Sta. Rosa approving the development permit in favor of your company, we are of the view that the said Resolution should not anymore be forwarded to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review since this kind of Resolution cannot be considered as a Resolution adopting the local development plan or public investment program. Said Resolution of the Sangguniang Panlungsod approving your company's development permit was an exercise of its powers, duties and functions pursuant to Section 458(2)(x) of the Local Government Code which provides and we quote: "SECTION 458. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation.—(a) The sangguniang panlungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the city as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: (2) Generate and maximize the use of resources and revenues for the development plans, program objectives and priorities of the city as provided for under Section 18 of this Code, with particular attention to agro-industrial development and city-wide growth and progress, and relative thereto, shall: (x) Subject to national law, process and approve subdivision plans for residential, commercial, or industrial purposes, and to collect processing fees and other charges, the proceeds of which shall accrue entirely to the city: Provided, however, That where approval of a national agency or office is required, said approval shall not be withheld for more than thirty (30) days from receipt of the application. Failure to act on the application within the period stated above shall be deemed as approval thereof." Hence, its submission to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan for review is not anymore necessary as it is not even a legal requirement under the Local Government Code. Accordingly, we believe that in the event that the Sangguniang Panlalawigan shall insist on reviewing the said Kapasiyahan No. 156-2008, series of 2008, the same will produce no legal force and effect since such review is not legally required by the Local Government Code. This goes without saying that we concur with the legal position of the Sangguniang Panlungsod as mentioned above.

-4- Moreover, it must be stressed that since a Development Permit had already been issued by City Mayor Arlene Arcillas Nazareno in your company's favor, only the courts can now invalidate or nullify the issued Development Permit. In reply to your additional query, we answer in the negative. We are of the view that neither the Sangguniang Panlalawigan nor the Provincial Governor has the authority to issue a cease and desist order (CDO) against your company vis-å-vis you real estate project considering that both the Sangguniang Panlalawigan and the Provincial Governor, upon issuance, do not exercise judicial or quasi-judicial power. This point was exemplified by the Supreme Court in the case of Simon. Commission pn Human Rights SCRA 117 (1994)]. The Supreme Court held therein that the Commission only possesses investigatorial powers so that it cannot issue a Cease and Desist Order (a semantic interplay for a restraining order) which prescinds from an adjudicative power. The Supreme Court further cited the case of Export Processing Zone Authority Commission Human Rights [208 SCRA 125] wherein it held, in part, and we quote: "Not being a court of justice, the CHR itself has no jurisdiction issue the writ, for a writ of preliminary injunction may only be issued 'by the judge of any court in which the action is pending [within his district], or by a Justice of the Court of Appeals, or of the Supreme Court. ***. A writ of preliminary injunction is an ancillary remedy. It is available only in a pending principal action, for the preservation or protection Of the rights and interest of a party thereto, and for no other purpose." Also, in the case of Laguna Lake Development Authority Court gf Appeals [251 SCRA 4? (1994)], the Supreme Court held that the authority of the Laguna Lake Development Authority to issue cease and desist order is implied in the exercise of its express powers under its charter, as a regulatory and quasi-judicial body. In view thereof. any attempt to prohibit or stop your company from further developing the subject real estate project may not be in accordance with the rules and jurisprudence cited above. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, AUS RE A. PANADE O Undersecretar Cc: Undersecretary Eduardo R_ Soliman Special Constituency Relations LMP Bldg. Ermin Garcia St., Cubao, OC Legal/17
